text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High queue depth + elevated tail latency for tenant 'acme-health' in dedicated pool pool-acme-vpc-1 (severity P1). Trigger: queue_depth>4000 and p99_latency>1200ms. Link: https://console.redwood/incident/INC-2026-0315-01

Sara: I'm on this. seeing a sustained request spike from a small subset of ACME endpoints, looks like one customer job is hammering the scheduler with many short-lived requests.

Matt: Any customer-facing impact reported?

Sara: ACME reported intermittent 504s a few minutes ago. Support opened a ticket and linked it here.

Lucas: Can we isolate? Which pool config are we using? I see pool-acme-vpc-1 is exclusive, 8xA100, scheduler: fair-share with max_batch_tokens=2048, max_concurrent_batches=6.

Jenny: If it's lots of short requests, small batches will be filled and then stall because max_concurrent_batches is limiting throughput. Might be queue thrashing.

Brian: Suggested immediate mitigation: temporary increase max_concurrent_batches and raise max_batch_tokens to allow larger batching across arrivals. Also consider enabling prefix KV cache for repeated prompts.

Sara: Doing quick mitigation: bumping max_concurrent_batches to 12 and max_batch_tokens to 4096 for pool-acme-vpc-1. Will monitor.

Sara: Command I'm running: ```
redwoodctl pools update pool-acme-vpc-1 \
  --scheduler.kv.max_batch_tokens=4096 \
  --scheduler.kv.max_concurrent_batches=12 
```

ops-bot: Deploy request accepted, rolling config to pool-acme-vpc-1 (change set id cs-4721). Will apply to all nodes.

Matt: While that's rolling, can we gate the traffic? ACME has a heavy background job hitting inference for 20k small queries/min. Can we apply a short-term request rate-limit for their API key?

Sara: Reached out to ACME ops via the ticket asking to pause the bulk job. They replied they can pause in 10 minutes but need a short window to flush.

Lucas: If they can't pause, we can apply a tenant-level throttle: ```
redwoodctl tenants throttle acme-health --rps=2000 --burst=5000
```

Jenny: Note: throttling will queue more requests on our side if we don't also increase queue depth or batching. We have to be careful to avoid shifting latency to the queue.

ops-bot: Config update applied to pool-acme-vpc-1 on node set [node-12,node-14,node-16]. It will take ~30s to warm.

Sara: Seeing immediate drop in p99 latency to ~650ms and queue depth halved to ~1800. Good.

Brian: Nice. Keep a close eye on error rate and CPU/GPU utilization. If batch size grows too large we'll hit memory pressure on kv caches.

Matt: Can we get a short postmortem stub for support so they can tell ACME what happened? Need timeline and mitigations.

Sara: I'll draft. Initial timeline: 1779001234 - incident triggered by queue_depth>4000 and p99>1200ms. 1779001240 - mitigation config change issued (max_batch_tokens, max_concurrent_batches). 1779001260 - ops-bot confirmed rollout. 1779001274 - p99 dropped to ~650ms. 1779001288 - ACME acknowledged pausing bulk job.

Lucas: Follow-up action items: 1) Add automatic adaptive knob for max_concurrent_batches when queue spike detected (pilot). 2) Add tenant-specific soft caps to detect abusive background jobs and alert growth early. 3) Run load replay on staging to tune max_batch_tokens per model shape.

Jenny: Also record the exact command flags in the incident log and the memory/cuda metrics snapshot. We need those for a proper RCA.

Sara: Logs snippet from scheduler at peak:
```
[1779001238] scheduler: enqueue request tenant=acme-health req_id=aa1b size=23 tokens
[1779001238] scheduler: batch formed id=bb7 size=12 tokens=276
[1779001241] scheduler: queue_depth=4123 p99=1246ms
[1779001242] scheduler: drop_prob=0.02 due_to=latency_sla
```

Brian: Can we add a canary rule to automatically increase max_batch_tokens by 2x for 60s when p99>1000ms and queue_depth>3000? That would be a low-risk mitigation.

Matt: Agree, but make it limited and auditable. No silent autoscaling of batch_tokens without an auditable change set.

Sara: For ACME specifically, I'm enabling a temporary tenant guardrail: per-minute job detection to alert at 5x normal per-key QPS. I'll put that as a short-term feature flag.

ops-bot: Tenant throttle applied: acme-health rps=2000 burst=5000.

Lucas: After throttle and knob change, GPU utilization smoothed from 96% busy to 78% and tail latencies stabilized.

Jenny: Good outcome. Next steps: schedule a tuning session with platform/reliability and the ACME SRE contact to dial permanent knobs (and consider model quantization recommendations).

Sara: I'm on the call with ACME at 18:30 UTC to walk through what happened and recommended changes; will attach notes.

Matt: Thanks all. Please add the incident tag INC-2026-0315-01 and create a short postmortem doc in /incidents/ after the initial RCA. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Follow-ups required: adaptive-knob (owner=lucas), tenant-guardrails (owner=sara), postmortem (owner=matt).
